summary: @hubsync/web-sdk-react preinstall downloads Bun and executes obfuscated payload; impersonates @verdocs/web-sdk-react
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts and chmods the binary, then invokes it against the sibling `math_init.js` — a 727KB single-blob file marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` containing a string-array rotation obfuscator with a ~1000-entry literal array and `push/shift` shuffler. The file has no source, no map, and no documented purpose. The package identifies itself as `@hubsync/web-sdk-react` while its description is 'Verdocs Web SDK for React' and its README instructs users to `npm i -S @verdocs/web-sdk-react`; the `@hubsync` scope is unrelated to Verdocs. The `dist/` tree appears to reuse Verdocs SDK code as a legitimate-looking wrapper around the added preinstall dropper. The alternate-runtime pattern (fetch a fresh interpreter, execute an opaque obfuscated sibling under it at install time) evades Node-only static and dynamic inspection; the impersonation of a real SDK provides the lure that gets developers to install it.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
